```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(Biostrings)
library(pwalign)
library(ape)
library(limma)

dir <- "data-raw/strain"
s16 <- readDNAStringSet(file.path(dir, "isolates_16s.fasta"))
kred_dna <- readDNAStringSet(file.path(dir, "isolates_kred.fasta"))
arr <- read.csv(file.path(dir, "process_array.csv"))
smp <- read.csv(file.path(dir, "process_samples.csv"))
fun <- read.csv(file.path(dir, "process_probes.csv"))

# PL-7's KRED protein, from the /translation of the kred CDS in the GenBank record (Lesson 2)
read_translation <- function(gb, gene) {
  from <- grep(paste0('/gene="', gene, '"'), gb)[1]
  t1 <- grep("/translation=", gb); t1 <- t1[t1 > from][1]
  t2 <- t1 - 1 + grep('"[[:space:]]*$', gb[t1:length(gb)])[1]
  gsub('[[:space:]"]|/translation=', "", paste(gb[t1:t2], collapse = ""))
}
kred_pl7 <- AAString(read_translation(readLines(file.path(dir, "pl7_fragment.gb")), "kred"))
catalytic <- c(S = 141, Y = 154, K = 158)   # positions in PL-7's KRED
motif <- 12:19                              # TGxxxGxG, the cofactor-binding motif
```

## 2. What are the isolates?

<!-- Lessons 4, 5, 8 and 9. Check each read's orientation, place the reads on a common
     coordinate system, compute distances, build a tree, and bootstrap it. -->

```{r}
#| label: orientation
#| eval: false
ref <- s16[["REF_Rhodococcus_PL7"]]
score <- function(x) pairwiseAlignment(x, ref, type = "global-local", scoreOnly = TRUE)
fwd <- sapply(seq_along(s16), function(i) score(s16[[i]]))
rev <- sapply(seq_along(s16), function(i) score(reverseComplement(s16[[i]])))
flip <- rev > fwd
names(s16)[flip]                                  # which reads are backwards?
s16[flip] <- reverseComplement(s16[flip])
```

```{r}
#| label: tree
#| eval: false
# The 16S reads differ only by substitutions and trimming, so each can be placed on the
# PL-7 reference's coordinates; aligned() pads the ends with gaps.
placed <- sapply(seq_along(s16), function(i) as.character(aligned(pairwiseAlignment(s16[[i]], ref, type = "global-local"))))
dna <- as.DNAbin(strsplit(setNames(placed, names(s16)), ""))
d <- dist.dna(dna, model = "K80", pairwise.deletion = TRUE)   # gaps and Ns are left out pair by pair
tree <- root(nj(d), "...", resolve.root = TRUE)                # which reference is the outgroup?
boots <- boot.phylo(tree, as.matrix(dna), function(x) root(nj(dist.dna(x, model = "K80", pairwise.deletion = TRUE)), "...", resolve.root = TRUE), B = 200, quiet = TRUE)
tree$node.label <- round(100 * boots / 200)
plot(tree, show.node.label = TRUE, cex = 0.8)
```

## 3. Which isolates carry an intact kred gene?

<!-- Lessons 1, 3 and 4. Translate each gene on both strands, align the protein with PL-7's KRED,
     and check the catalytic residues and the motif. What has gone wrong in the broken ones? -->

```{r}
#| label: kred
#| eval: false
n_stops <- function(p) sum(strsplit(as.character(p), "")[[1]] == "*")
check_one <- function(x) {
  f <- translate(x, if.fuzzy.codon = "X"); r <- translate(reverseComplement(x), if.fuzzy.codon = "X")
  strand <- if (n_stops(f) <= n_stops(r)) "+" else "-"
  p <- if (strand == "+") f else r
  aln <- pairwiseAlignment(AAString(sub("[*].*$", "", as.character(p))), kred_pl7,
                           substitutionMatrix = "BLOSUM62", gapOpening = 10, gapExtension = 0.5, type = "global-local")
  a <- strsplit(as.character(aligned(aln)), "")[[1]]          # the isolate's protein in PL-7's coordinates
  data.frame(strand = strand, stops = n_stops(p), identity = round(pid(aln), 1),
             S141 = a[catalytic["S"]], Y154 = a[catalytic["Y"]], K158 = a[catalytic["K"]],
             motif = paste(a[motif], collapse = ""))
}
kred_check <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(kred_dna), function(i) check_one(kred_dna[[i]])))
rownames(kred_check) <- names(kred_dna)
kred_check
# a gene with stops on both strands: align its DNA with PL-7's kred DNA (Lesson 2) to find out why
```

## 4. Which genes respond to high substrate load?

<!-- Lessons 12 and 13. Preprocess, handle the duplicated probes, check the arrays' quality and
     labels, then fit a linear model with limma. Think about the scan days. -->

```{r}
#| label: preprocess
#| eval: false
X <- as.matrix(arr[, smp$array])
B <- backgroundCorrect.matrix(X, method = "normexp", offset = 16, verbose = FALSE)
L <- avereps(log2(B), ID = arr$gene)                # one row per gene: duplicated probes averaged
N <- normalizeBetweenArrays(L, method = "quantile")
```

```{r}
#| label: qc
#| eval: false
round(cor(N), 3)                                   # does every array look like its own group?
pc <- prcomp(t(N))
plot(pc$x[, 1:2], type = "n"); text(pc$x[, 1:2], labels = colnames(N))
table(smp$load, smp$scan_day)                      # is the design balanced?
# if two arrays' labels are swapped, fix smp (and say why in the cleaning log)
```

```{r}
#| label: limma
#| eval: false
smp$load <- factor(smp$load, levels = c("low", "high"))   # so the coefficient is high vs low
design <- model.matrix(~ ... , data = smp)          # load, and the scan day?
fit <- eBayes(lmFit(N, design))
tt <- topTable(fit, coef = "loadhigh", number = Inf)
sum(tt$adj.P.Val < 0.05)
hist(tt$P.Value, breaks = 20)
top <- head(tt, 20)
cbind(round(top[, c("logFC", "AveExpr", "adj.P.Val")], 3), func = fun$func[match(rownames(top), fun$gene)])
```
